6
An experiment to determine atmospheric pressure P uses the equation P = ρ gh where
ρ = (13 600 ± 100) kg m–3,
g = (9.81 ± 0.02) m s–2,
h = (0.762 ± 0.005) m.
What is the value of P, with its uncertainty, when stated to an appropriate number of significant
figures?
Pa
A
(1.0166 ± 0.0162) × 105
B
(1.017 ± 0.016) × 105
Pa
C
(1.017 ± 1.6%) × 105
Pa
D
(1.02 ± 0.02) × 105
Pa

hints: Notice $P = \rho g h$ is a pure multiplication, so work out the three fractional uncertainties $100/13600$, $0.02/9.81$ and $0.005/0.762$ for $\rho$, $g$ and $h$.
Add those three percentage uncertainties to get about $1.6\%$ for $P$, then multiply by $P = 13600 \times 9.81 \times 0.762$ to get the absolute uncertainty in $\text{Pa}$.
Compare the size of the absolute uncertainty, about $0.016 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$, with the value $1.0166 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ to decide how many figures can be kept in both numbers.
walkthrough: Calculate the best value: $P = \rho g h = 13600 \times 9.81 \times 0.762 \approx 101660 \text{ Pa} = 1.0166 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$.
Calculate each fractional uncertainty: $\Delta \rho/\rho = 100/13600 \approx 0.74\%$, $\Delta g/g = 0.02/9.81 \approx 0.20\%$, $\Delta h/h = 0.005/0.762 \approx 0.66\%$.
For multiplication add fractional uncertainties: $\Delta P/P \approx 0.74\% + 0.20\% + 0.66\% \approx 1.6\%$.
Convert to absolute uncertainty: $\Delta P \approx 0.016 \times 1.0166 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa} \approx 0.0162 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$.

Round for appropriate significant figures: an uncertainty of $0.0162 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ rounds to one significant figure as $0.02 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$, so $P$ must be rounded to the same $0.01 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ place as $1.02 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$.
Combine as $(1.02 \pm 0.02) \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Gives the unrounded calculation $P = 1.0166 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ and $1620 \text{ Pa}$ uncertainty, which keeps too many significant figures for the $1.6\%$ total uncertainty.

B.explanation: Correctly finds about $1.6\%$ uncertainty but keeps the value to 4 significant figures while the absolute uncertainty $0.016 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ is only known to the second decimal place of $10^5 \text{ Pa}$.

C.explanation: Correctly finds about $1.6\%$ fractional uncertainty but the value $1.017 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ is quoted to too many figures and mixes absolute and percentage form inconsistently.

D.explanation: Rounds the $1.6\%$ uncertainty to one significant figure, $0.02 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$, and matches $P$ to the same place as $1.02 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$.
